executive_summary: Development encompasses material aspirations (higher income, employment) as well as non-material goals like freedom, security, equal treatment, and respect. Relying solely on per capita income ignores income distribution and essential human indicators like literacy, life expectancy, and infant mortality.

storyboard.title: Different People, Different Goals
storyboard.description: Visualizing how an industrialist's goal of building a hydro dam conflicts directly with a tribal community's goal of preserving their ancestral land.
storyboard.key_takeaway: Developmental goals can be distinct and mutually conflicting.

storyboard.title: Income vs. Human Indicators
storyboard.description: Comparing Haryana's higher income with Kerala's superior health (IMR 7) and education (94% literacy) metrics.
storyboard.key_takeaway: Money cannot buy essential public healthcare and social security.

storyboard.title: Ecological Balance & Sustainability
storyboard.description: Illustrating groundwater table collapse in agricultural states and global crude oil depletion.
storyboard.key_takeaway: Present development must maintain inter-generational equity.

video_embeds.title: Understanding Human Development Index & PCI
video_embeds.transcript_summary: Explains the difference between World Bank Per Capita Income criteria and UNDP HDI composite metrics.

hotspots.popover_content: Material vs Non-Material goals. Example: Dam construction creating power for industrialists while displacing indigenous riverine tribes.
Per Capita Income = Total Income / Population. World Bank threshold: Rich > $49,300 vs Low <= $2,500. UNDP HDI incorporates health and education.

key_takeaways: Development requires income plus non-material dignity, safety, and freedom.
Public facilities are essential for human capital development.
Resources must be managed sustainably to protect future generations.
